newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: RESEARCH ALERT-Yukong upgraded to "buy".
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Yukong upgraded to "buy".

text.p: ING-Baring Securities in Seoul said on Friday it was upgrading its recommendation for refiner Yukong Ltd to "buy" from "long-term buy" due to its improving margins and attractive valuations.

"We have upgraded our earnings to account for both improved refining margins and to reflect the capitalising of its foreign exchange translation loss on long-term foreign debt from 1996," the brokerage said in a report.
It also said its 12-month target price for the stock was 25,000 won per share, compared with 16,800 won at present.

In the wake of strong oil price growth during 1996, coupled with government intervention to bring local refined product prices in line with international prices, Yukong's average total product value per barrel rose by 31 percent year-on-year in 1996, it said.

Margins are likely to improve this year in light of the better-than-expected impact of the January 1 deregulation that allowed companies to raise refined product prices with little interference from the government, the report said.

The brokerage said net profit of the nation's largest oil refiner was forecast to rise to 136 billion won in 1997 from an estimated 94 billion won in 1996 and sales to rise to 9.42 trillion won from 8.42 trillion.
